P0400.title: EGR A Flow
P0400.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0400 is the general flow fault of EGR system A, used where the module does not classify the error as too little (P0401) or too much (P0402). Ford petrol engines with a stepper-motor valve open and close the valve at steady part load and compare intake manifold pressure with and without EGR; too small a normalised difference (below 1.0) sets P0400, MIL after two trips. GM diesels use the code differently, for air-mass checks with excessive EGR rate. EGR is then usually switched off.

causes.label: EGR passages or valve carboned up
EGR valve stiff or faulty
Leak in the intake or EGR pipe
MAP or MAF sensor inaccurate

symptoms: Pinging under load or rough idle, depending on direction

P0401.title: EGR A Flow Insufficient Detected
P0401.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0401 means too little exhaust is recirculated. Petrol engines open the valve briefly and expect a rise in manifold pressure (GM 2004 V6, MIL on the first trip); older Ford systems measure the pressure drop across an orifice (DPFE sensor). Diesels balance the air mass: if the meter sees more fresh air than the target EGR rate allows, too little exhaust flows (GM, Ford, Saab, usually MIL after two trips). Diesel causes are mostly a coked valve or cooler, petrol causes blocked passages.

causes.label: EGR passages, valve or cooler carboned up
EGR valve faulty or stuck closed
Ford: DPFE sensor or its hoses blocked, cracked or swapped
Diesel: air mass meter drifting or air leak after the turbo
Vacuum control of the valve faulty

P0402.title: EGR A Flow Excessive Detected
P0402.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0402 means too much exhaust is recirculated, or exhaust flows although the valve should be closed – CARB explicitly requires a leaking valve to be detected. Ford's DPFE check at idle with EGR off expects no pressure difference above the engine-off value; Ford diesels compare the measured EGR rate with the expected one, GM diesels the fresh-air deviation in the opposite direction. Petrol engines idle roughly or stall, diesels smoke and may lose power.

causes.label: EGR valve stuck open, dirt under the seat
Ford: DPFE sensor drifting or hose wrong
Diesel: air leak between air mass meter and turbo, MAF drift
Valve control opens unintentionally

symptoms: Diesel: black smoke, loss of power

P0403.title: EGR A Control Circuit/Open
P0403.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0403 concerns the electrical drive of the EGR valve – solenoid, stepper motor, DC motor or vacuum regulator. The module checks the output and sets the code for an open circuit (GM: above 200 kΩ, MIL after two trips; Ford after 4 s, MIL after two trips). Newer systems report shorts separately as P0489 (low) and P0490 (high); Ford and older GM systems include them in P0403. EGR is then switched off for the rest of the trip.

causes.label: Connector at the EGR valve corroded or loose
Broken control or supply wire
Coil or motor in the EGR valve burnt out
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: EGR switched off: pinging (petrol) or higher NOx

P0404.title: EGR A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0404.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0404 is the function check of the valve drive: on valves with a position sensor the module compares commanded and actual position, and a persistent deviation means the valve sticks, is coked or its drive is too weak (GM diesel 2018 above 10 %, GM petrol 2004 above 15 %, both MIL after two trips). Ford calls it control stuck. Saab's V6 diesel deviates and uses P0404 for a short to positive. EGR control is then switched off and the valve de-energised.

causes.label: Valve coked or stiff
Valve drive (motor, gear) worn
Position sensor in the valve inaccurate
Supply voltage too low or ground fault

symptoms: Rough idle or jerking if the valve hangs open

P0405.title: EGR Sensor A Circuit Low
P0405.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR sensor A is usually the valve position sensor with a 5 V supply; on Ford until about 2011 it was the DPFE differential pressure sensor. P0405 means its signal is below the lower limit – GM 2018 below 11 % of 5 V (MIL after two trips), Ford below 5 % of full scale for 4 s, Saab below 0.26 V. The cause is a short to ground or an open signal or 5 V wire. EGR position control is then switched off.

causes.label: Wire or connector to the EGR valve open or shorted to ground
Position sensor in the EGR valve faulty (usually one unit with the valve)
Older Ford: DPFE sensor faulty
Shared 5 V reference shorted

P0406.title: EGR Sensor A Circuit High
P0406.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR sensor A is usually the valve position sensor; on Ford until about 2011 the DPFE differential pressure sensor. P0406 means its signal is above the upper limit – GM 2018 above 97.7 % of 5 V, GM 2005 above 94.7 % (both MIL after two trips), Ford petrol above 95 % for 4 s, Ford diesel above 4.70 V, Saab above 4.75 V. Typical is a signal wire shorted to positive or an open sensor ground, which GM names explicitly. EGR is then switched off.

causes.label: Sensor ground or return wire open
Signal wire shorted to 5 V or positive
Sensor in the EGR valve faulty
Moisture or corrosion in the connector

P0407.title: EGR Sensor B Circuit Low
P0407.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor B is depends on the manufacturer – on systems with a second valve or pressure sensor it is that second sensor. GM's diesels of 2017/18 use P0407 for the coolant temperature sensor at the inlet of the high-pressure EGR cooler: low means a resistance below 55 Ω, i.e. very hot or shorted to ground, MIL after two trips. No manufacturer document available to us uses the code for a second position sensor. A substitute value is used.

causes.label: Sensor wire shorted to ground
Sensor faulty
Connector corroded (near coolant or exhaust)
Engine module input

symptoms: EGR or EGR cooler protection possibly restricted

P0408.title: EGR Sensor B Circuit High
P0408.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor B is depends on the manufacturer – on systems with a second valve or pressure sensor it is that second sensor. GM's diesels of 2017/18 use P0408 for the coolant temperature sensor at the inlet of the high-pressure EGR cooler: high means a resistance above 134 kΩ, i.e. an open circuit or extreme cold (20 of 24 samples, MIL after two trips). A substitute value is used.

causes.label: Signal or ground wire open, connector off
Sensor faulty
Connector corroded (near coolant or exhaust)
Engine module input

symptoms: EGR or EGR cooler protection possibly restricted

P0409.title: EGR Sensor A Circuit
P0409.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR sensor A is usually the valve position sensor (on older Fords the DPFE pressure sensor). P0409 is its general circuit code, for a missing or implausible signal that the module does not classify as low or high. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – GM, Ford and Saab report sensor A as P0405/P0406, Ford intermittent faults as P046D – so the description follows CARB, which requires input circuits to be checked for continuity and range. EGR is usually switched off.

causes.label: Connector or wire of the position sensor open or loose
EGR valve with integrated sensor faulty
5 V reference or ground disturbed
Engine module

P040A.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P040A.description: EGR temperature sensor A measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it. Like a coolant sensor it is an NTC, so a low voltage means hot. P040A is its general circuit code. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – GM and Ford report this sensor as P040B to P040E – so the description follows CARB's requirement to check input circuits for continuity and range. A substitute value is used and the EGR cooler check is suspended.

causes.label: Connector or wire at the sensor (heat, corrosion)
Sensor faulty
Engine module input

symptoms: Substitute value used, EGR cooler check suspended

P040B.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P040B.description: EGR temperature sensor A measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it. Like a coolant sensor it is an NTC, so a low voltage means hot. P040B is its plausibility check: after a cold start the sensor must warm up once hot exhaust flows. Ford diesels set the code if it rises by less than 10 °C after load; GM diesels if it barely changes after at least 8 hours off and a defined EGR flow (MIL after two trips). A sooted sensor tip or a lack of EGR flow are typical causes.

causes.label: Sensor sluggish, tip sooted
Sensor drifting or faulty
No EGR flow (valve or cooler blocked), sensor sees no heat
Contact resistance in the connector

symptoms: Substitute value used, EGR cooler check suspended

P040C.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P040C.description: EGR temperature sensor A measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it. Like a coolant sensor it is an NTC, so a low voltage means hot. P040C means the signal is below its lower limit – very hot or a signal wire shorted to ground. Thresholds: GM's Duramax LML below 0.46 V for 5 s, GM 2014 below 0.14 V, GM 2018 a resistance below 404 Ω, Ford diesel below 0.69 V for 5 s; MIL after two trips. A substitute value is used and the EGR cooler check is suspended.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground (chafed on the exhaust)
Sensor shorted internally
Water in the connector
Actual extreme gas temperature (EGR cooler faulty)

symptoms: Substitute value used, EGR cooler check suspended

P040D.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P040D.description: EGR temperature sensor A measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it. Like a coolant sensor it is an NTC, so a low voltage means hot. P040D means the signal is above its upper limit – very cold or, far more often, an open circuit (connector off, broken wire). Thresholds: GM's Duramax LML above 4.84 V for 5 s, GM 2014 above 4.98 V, GM 2018 a resistance above 1268 Ω (40 of 50 samples, MIL after two trips); Ford diesel lists the code without figures. A substitute value is used.

causes.label: Connector off, broken wire or open circuit
Sensor open internally
Ground wire open or short to positive
Engine module input

symptoms: Substitute value used, EGR cooler check suspended

P040E.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P040E.description: EGR temperature sensor A measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it. Like a coolant sensor it is an NTC, so a low voltage means hot. P040E means the signal jumps. GM diesels of 2016–18 set it when the measured resistance changes by more than 25 Ω between two samples 100 ms apart – faster than any real temperature change, so a loose contact or a cracked sensor is the cause (40 of 50 samples, MIL after two trips). Ford and GM's earlier Duramax LML do not use the code.

causes.label: Loose contact in the connector or chafed wire
Sensor with an internal hairline crack
Corroded pins

symptoms: Check engine light on, may come and go

P040F.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A/B Correlation
P040F.description: The two EGR temperature sensors measure the gas temperature in the EGR path, before and after the cooler – which is A and which is B depends on the maker. P040F compares sensors A and B: after a long stop (GM: at least 8 hours) both must read about ambient temperature. If they differ by more than the calibrated limit at start-up (GM Duramax LML table, at least 20 °C, with exclusions for block heaters), the code is set, MIL after two trips. It does not say which sensor is wrong – compare both with intake air and coolant temperature. Ford diesels cover the same goal with P041B.

causes.label: One sensor drifting
Contact resistance at one sensor's connector
Connectors swapped after a repair
Unrecognised heat source (auxiliary heater)

symptoms: Check engine light on, may come and go

P0410.title: AIR System A
P0410.description: After a cold start the secondary air (AIR) pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; a shut-off valve opens the path and stops exhaust from flowing back. P0410 is the general function code for secondary air system A. Many Bosch-managed engines check it passively: with the pump running, the front oxygen sensor must read lean or the fuel control must react; Pierburg lists P0410 as no lean signal, i.e. no air detected. Saab's Motronic 900, by contrast, uses it for too much air. GM's systems with a pressure sensor use P0411 and P2440 ff instead. The check runs once per trip after a cold start; driving is unaffected.

causes.label: Secondary air pump failed (water ingress, seized)
Combination or shut-off valve carboned up or stuck
Vacuum hose or electric changeover valve leaking or faulty
Pump relay or fuse faulty
Air ducts in the head carboned up or hose off

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)
Pump silent after a cold start, or unusually loud

P0411.title: AIR System A Incorrect Flow Detected
P0411.description: After a cold start the secondary air (AIR) pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; a shut-off valve opens the path and stops exhaust from flowing back. P0411 means the measured air flow does not match the expected value. Passive systems judge it from the oxygen sensor or fuel control (Saab 900: less than 12 points of correction within 12 s). GM measures actively with a pressure sensor between pump and valve and compares it with a model while pump and valve are on – from 2018 a deviation above 5.0 kPa or below −4.9 kPa sets the code, MIL after two trips. The test needs a cold engine after a long stop, so short warm trips do not complete it.

causes.label: Pump weak or failed (water, filter debris)
Combination valve partly stuck or check valve faulty
Hoses blocked, leaking or off; ducts in the head carboned up
Pressure sensor port blocked or sensor drifting (pressure-sensor systems)
Pump relay or supply with contact resistance

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)
Pump silent after a cold start, or unusually loud

P0412.title: AIR System Switching Valve A Circuit
P0412.description: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. P0412 is the general electrical fault in the control circuit of valve A, detected by comparing the driver's feedback with its commanded state. GM has used it since about 2015 specifically for an open circuit (200 kΩ or more, 20 of 25 samples, MIL after two trips) and reports shorts as P041F and P044F; older GM systems and Toyota use it for any driver fault. The valve then stays shut, so secondary air is missing and P0411 or P2441 may follow.

causes.label: Switching valve A faulty (coil open or shorted, water ingress)
Connector corroded or wire open or chafed
Valve supply missing (fuse, main relay)
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)

P0413.title: AIR System Switching Valve A Circuit Open
P0413.description: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. P0413 means the control circuit of valve A is open: with the driver switched off the module does not see the expected supply or pull-up level. The check runs continuously. Subaru's two-valve system assigns valve A to bank 1, and its bulletin advises checking the valve of the other bank as well. The valve stays shut and the bank gets no secondary air; flow codes such as P0411 may follow.

causes.label: Wire to the valve open or connector loose or corroded
Valve coil burnt out
Fuse of the valve supply blown
Engine module

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)

P0414.title: AIR System Switching Valve A Circuit Shorted
P0414.description: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. P0414 means the control circuit of valve A is shorted. A short to ground keeps the valve energized and open; a short to supply or a shorted coil overloads the driver, which many modules then switch off for the rest of the trip. An open valve with the pump running can also set P2440, and exhaust can reach the pump if the check valve leaks. Subaru names P0414 in its bulletin for the two-valve system.

causes.label: Valve coil with shorted turns (water ingress)
Wire chafed against ground or supply
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)

P0415.title: AIR System Switching Valve B Circuit
P0415.description: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. P0415 is the general electrical fault in the control circuit of valve B, the second valve on two-valve or two-bank systems such as V engines or Subaru's turbo boxer. It is detected like P0412 for valve A, by comparing the driver's feedback with its commanded state. No manufacturer document available to us describes P0415 specifically; Pierburg's fault table lists it with the same remedies as valve A.

causes.label: Switching valve B faulty
Wire or connector to valve B faulty
Valve supply or fuse
Engine module

symptoms: Secondary air inactive on the second bank
Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)

P0416.title: AIR System Switching Valve B Circuit Open
P0416.description: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. P0416 means the control circuit of valve B is open – the module does not see the expected level with its driver switched off. On Subaru's two-valve system valve B serves bank 2; the bulletin advises checking the valve of the other bank too, because a shared supply can be the cause. The valve stays shut and that bank gets no secondary air.

causes.label: Wire or connector to valve B open
Coil of valve B burnt out
Shared supply of both valves faulty
Engine module

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)

P0417.title: AIR System Switching Valve B Circuit Shorted
P0417.description: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. P0417 means the control circuit of valve B is shorted. As with valve A (P0414), a short to ground keeps the valve open, while a short to supply or a shorted coil overloads the driver, which is then often switched off for the rest of the trip. Subaru names P0417 for its two-valve system, with valve B on bank 2.

causes.label: Coil of valve B with shorted turns (water ingress)
Wire chafed against ground or supply
Connector corroded
Engine module

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)

P0418.title: AIR System Control A Circuit
P0418.description: After a cold start the secondary air (AIR) pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; a shut-off valve opens the path and stops exhaust from flowing back. Control A is the drive circuit of pump A – in practice the coil of the pump relay, which the module switches to ground; the old wording was Relay A. GM uses P0418 for an open circuit (200 kΩ or more, 20 of 25 samples, MIL after two trips) and P2257/P2258 for shorts; Saab and Toyota describe the same circuit. If the pump does not run, P0411 may follow. A relay with welded contacts keeps the pump running – Subaru recalled cars because the pump could overheat.

causes.label: Pump relay faulty (coil open, contacts burnt or welded)
Control wire or connector to the relay open or corroded
Fuse blown, often due to a seized pump
Pump stiff or blocked by water or debris
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Pump does not run after a cold start – or runs constantly if the relay is welded
Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)
Hot pump or burning smell if it runs constantly

P0419.title: AIR System Control B Circuit
P0419.description: After a cold start the secondary air (AIR) pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; a shut-off valve opens the path and stops exhaust from flowing back. Control B is the drive circuit of a second pump or pump relay, found only on systems with two pumps or relays, for example large V engines with one pump per bank. It is checked like P0418 by comparing the driver's feedback with its commanded state. No manufacturer document available to us describes P0419 specifically; Pierburg's fault table lists it as relay B with the same remedies as relay A.

causes.label: Pump relay B faulty
Wire or connector to relay B faulty
Fuse or supply
Pump B blocked (consequential damage)
Engine module

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)

P041A.title: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit
P041A.description: EGR temperature sensor B measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it. Like a coolant sensor it is an NTC, so a low voltage means hot. P041A is its general circuit code. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – GM and Ford report sensor B as P041B to P041D – so the description follows CARB's requirement to check input circuits for continuity and range. A substitute value is used and the EGR cooler check is suspended.

causes.label: Connector or wire at the sensor
Sensor faulty
Engine module input

symptoms: Substitute value used, EGR cooler check suspended

P041B.title: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P041B.description: EGR temperature sensor B measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it. Like a coolant sensor it is an NTC, so a low voltage means hot. P041B is its plausibility check. Ford diesels compare it at a cold start, after at least 6 hours off, with two other air temperatures (limit 25 °C, 30 °C with a block heater); GM diesels set the code if it barely changes after 8 hours off and EGR operation. Ford petrol engines list P041B with the electrical checks (5 s). MIL after two trips.

causes.label: Sensor drifting or sluggish (soot)
Contact resistance in the connector
No EGR flow (GM stuck test)
Comparison sensor (intake or charge air temperature) faulty

symptoms: Substitute value used, EGR cooler check suspended

P041C.title: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low
P041C.description: EGR temperature sensor B measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it. Like a coolant sensor it is an NTC, so a low voltage means hot. P041C means the signal is below its lower limit – very hot or shorted to ground; Ford puts below 0.10 V at about 961 °C. Thresholds: Ford diesel below 0.10 V for 3 s, Ford petrol below 0.32 V for 5 s, GM's Duramax LML below 0.46 V for 5 s, GM 2018 a resistance below 164 Ω; MIL after two trips. A substitute value is used and the EGR cooler check (P2457) is suspended.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor shorted internally
Moisture in the connector
Actual overtemperature (cooler or coolant problem)

symptoms: Substitute value used, EGR cooler check suspended

P041D.title: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit High
P041D.description: EGR temperature sensor B measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it. Like a coolant sensor it is an NTC, so a low voltage means hot. P041D means the signal is above its upper limit – very cold or, far more often, an open circuit; Ford puts above 4.90 V at about −46 °C. Thresholds: Ford diesel above 4.90 V, Ford petrol above 4.94 V for 5 s, GM's Duramax LML above 4.84 V, GM 2018 a resistance above 859 Ω; MIL after two trips. A substitute value is used and the EGR cooler check is suspended.

causes.label: Connector off or broken wire
Sensor open internally
Ground open or short to positive
Engine module

symptoms: Substitute value used, EGR cooler check suspended

P041E.title: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P041E.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR temperature sensor B is the second temperature sensor in the EGR path; on GM diesels it sits before the cooler, on Ford diesels after it. P041E means its signal jumps. GM's diesels of 2016–18, the only documented users, set it when the measured resistance changes by more than 25 Ω between two samples 100 ms apart – faster than any real temperature change, so a loose contact or cracked sensor is the cause (40 of 50 samples, MIL after two trips). Dependent checks such as EGR cooler efficiency are then suspended.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector
Harness chafed or broken (heat at the EGR pipe)
Sensor cracked internally (thermal cycling)
Engine module or ground connection

symptoms: Check engine light on, may come and go
Further EGR temperature or cooler checks suspended

P041F.title: AIR System Switching Valve A Circuit Low
P041F.description: After a cold start the secondary air pump blows fresh air into the exhaust; switching valve A is the electrically driven valve that opens this path. GM checks the valve circuit in three codes – P0412 open, P041F shorted to ground, P044F shorted to positive – while other makers use P0413/P0414 or P0412 for everything. P041F means the control circuit is shorted to ground: GM checks with the driver switched off and sets the code at 0.5 Ω or less to ground (20 of 25 samples of 250 ms, above 11 V, MIL after two trips). The valve is then energised and open although not commanded; P0411 or P2440 may follow.

causes.label: Control wire chafed against ground
Water or corrosion in the valve connector
Valve coil shorted to its housing
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Check engine light on (after two trips)
Secondary air readiness not set, possibly P0411

P0420.title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
P0420.description: The engine module checks whether the catalyst of bank 1 still converts enough. On petrol engines it estimates the oxygen storage capacity by comparing the sensors before and after the catalyst – a good catalyst smooths the rear signal. GM uses a test on overrun (ratio below 0.35 sets the code on the first trip), Ford an index ratio above 0.75 or fuel integration after fuel cut-off. On diesels P0420 concerns the oxidation catalyst, checked by its heat release during filter regeneration (GM Duramax LML, Ford below 45 % of the expected heat). Ford names oil-borne poisoning as the most common cause.

causes.label: Catalyst aged or poisoned (oil consumption, silicone, coolant)
Catalyst overheated by misfire or rich running
Rear oxygen sensor sluggish, dirty or unsuitable
Exhaust leak ahead of or at the rear sensor
Diesel: oxidation catalyst sooted or poisoned, post-injection faulty

symptoms: Check engine light on, otherwise often no change in driving
Emission test failed (higher HC, CO, NOx)
Rattling or loss of power if the catalyst has broken up

P0421.title: Catalyst 1 Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
P0421.description: Catalyst 1 is the first catalyst in the flow direction of bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1) – the close-coupled or warm-up catalyst that lights off first after a cold start; the older wording was Warm Up Catalyst. P0421 means it no longer converts enough. Mitsubishi V6 engines with manifold catalysts and GM's 3.0/3.2-litre V6 of 2004/05 with Bosch control report it: the rear sensor amplitude is compared with a model, and a quality factor above 0.625 (2004) or 0.375 (2005) sets the code after two trips. GM's small diesels use P0421 for the close-coupled oxidation catalyst, tested by heat balance during filter regeneration.

P043E.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Reference Orifice Low Flow
P043E.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Systems with a leak detection pump (Bosch DM-TL at VW, Audi, BMW and Maserati, Denso's canister pump module at Toyota/Lexus) first measure a reference value with the pump working only through a built-in 0.5 mm (0.020 in) orifice; it is the yardstick for the small-leak test that CARB requires. P043E means the reference measurement shows too little flow – the vacuum (or with DM-TL the pressure and pump current) becomes stronger than expected, so the orifice or reference path is partly blocked, often by dirt or liquid after overfilling. GM and Ford do not use the code; Maserati fixed false triggering with software.

symptoms: EVAP leak test does not run, readiness not set

symptoms: Readiness or emission inspection not passed

P0441.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0441 means the actual purge flow does not match the target – too little, or flow although the purge valve is closed. CARB requires a fault when no purge flow is detected. Strategies differ widely: Saab's Trionic T7/T8 sets it for flow with the valve closed (tank pressure falling faster than 27.5–40 Pa/s), VW and Audi check purge flow with the leak detection pump, Honda/Acura for a sticking purge valve. GM and Ford do not use P0441 – they report flow with the valve closed as P0496 or P1450 and missing flow as P0455.

causes.label: Purge valve stuck open or not sealing
Purge valve stuck closed, purge line blocked, kinked or off
Leak detection pump with tolerance fault (VW)
Canister saturated or damaged, turbo purge check valve faulty

symptoms: Rough idle or hard start after refuelling (valve stuck open)

P0442.title: EVAP System Leak Detected (small leak)
P0442.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0442 reports a small leak; what size that means depends on the maker. Ford detects 0.040 in (1 mm) with the engine running: the vent valve closes, engine vacuum pulls the tank down, the purge valve closes and a pressure rise above 2.5 inH2O in 15 s sets the code (0.020 in is P0456). GM uses the natural pressure change after switch-off for 0.020 in and averages several tests. Pump systems at VW and Audi compare against a reference leak. A worn or loose fuel cap is the most common cause.

causes.label: Fuel cap seal worn, wrong or not clicked in
Cracked or porous EVAP hoses or leaking connections
Purge or vent valve does not seal
Leak detection pump itself leaking (VW/Audi)
Filler neck corroded, tank or sender seal leaking

symptoms: Readiness or emission inspection not passed

P0443.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit
P0443.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0443 is the electrical check of purge valve A, which the module switches to ground in pulses; it compares the driver's feedback voltage with the commanded state. GM uses it for an open circuit (200 kΩ or more, 20 of 25 samples, MIL after two trips) and reports shorts as P0458/P0459; Ford covers open and short in P0443 (5 s). Purging then stops, the canister is no longer regenerated, and the leak and purge monitors are suspended.

causes.label: Purge valve connector corroded, loose or off
Purge valve coil open or shorted
Control wire broken or chafed, or supply missing (fuse, main relay)
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: EVAP leak test does not run

P0444.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit Open
P0444.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0444 belongs to the older scheme of circuit, open and shorted codes for purge valve A; Saab's Trionic T7 and VW use it, while GM reports an open circuit as P0443 and Ford covers everything in P0443. Saab checks with the output switched off: below 2 V the supply through the coil is missing or the line is grounded – Saab combines both under P0444, sets it after about 1 s and pauses the check until the next drive. Purging then stops.

causes.label: Purge valve connector off or corroded
Valve coil open
Supply wire, fuse, main relay or control wire open
Control wire shorted to ground (Saab definition)

P0445.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit Shorted
P0445.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0445 is the short-circuit code of the older scheme for purge valve A, used by Saab's Trionic T7 and VW; GM reports shorts as P0458/P0459, Ford covers them in P0443. Saab checks with the low-side output switched on: the voltage should then be near 0 V, and above 2 V means the line is shorted to positive or the coil is shorted, with the driver in current limiting. The code sets after about 1 s; the driver protects itself by switching off, so purging stops.

causes.label: Purge valve coil shorted (shorted turns)
Control wire shorted to positive (chafed)
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver in the engine module

P0446.title: EVAP System Vent Control Circuit
P0446.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The vent valve is normally open and closes for the leak test. By its wording P0446 is its control circuit, and Ford uses it that way for open and shorted circuits. GM, however, uses P0446 for vent system performance – a blocked vent path: while purging with the vent valve open, the tank must not build up vacuum; more than 2989 Pa for 5 s before 4 litres have been purged sets the code, MIL after two trips. GM reports vent circuit faults as P0449, P0498 and P0499. A blocked vent makes refuelling difficult.

causes.label: Vent valve or filter blocked by dirt, dust or water (GM reading)
Vent valve electrically faulty, coil open or shorted (Ford reading)
Connector or wire to the vent valve corroded or open
Canister clogged with charcoal or liquid (overfilling)
Vent hose kinked or blocked by an insect nest

symptoms: Refuelling problems, nozzle clicks off early (blocked vent)
Hissing when opening the fuel cap (vacuum)
EVAP leak test does not run

P0447.title: EVAP System Vent Control Circuit Open
P0447.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0447 belongs to the older scheme for the vent valve circuit (P0446 circuit, P0447 open, P0448 shorted), used by Subaru (also in the Saab 9-2X), VW and Nissan; GM reports an open vent circuit as P0449, Ford as P0446. On Subaru the valve is fed from the main relay and switched to ground by the module; if the voltage at the module output is missing or the coil is high-resistance (nominal 10–100 Ω), the code sets after two consecutive drives. The valve stays in its rest position and the leak test cannot run.

causes.label: Vent valve connector corroded or off (underbody, splash water)
Vent valve coil open (resistance outside 10–100 Ω)
Wire to the module or supply from the main relay open
Engine module or its connector

symptoms: EVAP leak test does not run, readiness not set

P0448.title: EVAP System Vent Control Circuit Shorted
P0448.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0448 is the short-circuit code of the older scheme for the vent valve. Subaru (also in the Saab 9-2X) expects supply voltage above 10 V at the module output with the valve off; a short to positive or a coil below 1 Ω sets the code after two drives, and Subaru then also replaces the module, as its driver may be damaged. Nissan and Infiniti use P0448 differently, for a vent valve or vent path stuck closed by dust or water, with replacement of canister, valve and filler tube. GM and Ford do not use the code.

causes.label: Vent valve or vent path blocked by dust, dirt or water (Nissan reading)
Vent valve coil shorted (below 1 Ω)
Control wire shorted to positive
Module driver damaged

symptoms: Refuelling problems if the vent is blocked
EVAP leak test does not run

P0449.title: EVAP System Vent Valve Control Circuit/Open
P0449.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0449 belongs to the newer scheme for the vent valve circuit – P0449 open, P0498 low, P0499 high – used mainly by GM and also by VW. The normally open valve is fed from the battery and switched to ground; with the driver off, the output should show supply voltage. A floating 2.6–4.6 V, or an impedance of 200 kΩ or more, means an open circuit (GM: 20 of 25 samples, MIL after two trips). The leak test and the vent performance check P0446 are then suspended; purging continues.

causes.label: Vent valve connector (usually at the canister or tank, underbody) corroded or loose
Vent valve coil open
Supply (fuse) or control wire open
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: EVAP leak test does not run, readiness not set

P044A.title: EGR Sensor C Circuit
P044A.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor C is depends on the maker: on Ford petrol engines from 2020 it is the DPFE sensor, which measures the pressure drop across an orifice in the EGR pipe (sensor A there is the valve position sensor); GM diesels assign it to the position sensor of a low-pressure EGR valve, but only within fault groups. P044A is the general circuit fault of this sensor. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – Ford splits it into P044C/P044D – so the description follows CARB's requirement to check input circuits for continuity and range. Without the sensor, EGR flow and cooler checks are suspended.

causes.label: Connector or wire to sensor C open or corroded
Sensor faulty
5 V reference or ground disturbed (with other sensor codes)
Engine module

symptoms: EGR readiness not set, EGR possibly switched off

P044B.title: EGR Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P044B.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor C is depends on the maker: on Ford petrol engines from 2020 it is the DPFE sensor, which measures the pressure drop across an orifice in the EGR pipe (sensor A there is the valve position sensor); GM diesels assign it to the position sensor of a low-pressure EGR valve, but only within fault groups. P044B means its signal is electrically valid but implausible – for example a pressure difference with the valve closed, or no reaction when it opens. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; Ford checks the DPFE plausibility under its own codes P139A–P139C (hoses swapped, front or rear hose off or blocked). EGR flow diagnosis is then suspended.

causes.label: Pressure hoses off, swapped or blocked (soot, condensate)
Sensor zero point drifted
Orifice or EGR pipe coked
Contact resistance in the connector

symptoms: EGR readiness not set, EGR possibly switched off

P044C.title: EGR Sensor C Circuit Low
P044C.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor C is depends on the maker: on Ford petrol engines from 2020 it is the DPFE sensor, which measures the pressure drop across an orifice in the EGR pipe (sensor A there is the valve position sensor); GM diesels assign it to the position sensor of a low-pressure EGR valve, but only within fault groups. P044C means its signal is below the lower limit. Ford petrol engines from 2020 set it below 0.25 V for 5 s – a value the sensor cannot produce, since 0.5 V already means −11 kPa – so the signal is shorted to ground, the 5 V supply is open or the sensor is faulty. EGR flow, hose and cooler checks are then suspended; MIL after two trips.

causes.label: 5 V supply of the sensor open or shorted to ground
Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor faulty internally
Connector corroded or off

symptoms: EGR readiness not set, EGR possibly switched off

P044D.title: EGR Sensor C Circuit High
P044D.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor C is depends on the maker: on Ford petrol engines from 2020 it is the DPFE sensor, which measures the pressure drop across an orifice in the EGR pipe (sensor A there is the valve position sensor); GM diesels assign it to the position sensor of a low-pressure EGR valve, but only within fault groups. P044D means its signal is above the upper limit. Ford petrol engines from 2020 set it above 4.65 V for 5 s, beyond the measuring range that ends at 4.5 V (about +18 kPa) – typically an open sensor ground, a signal shorted to 5 V or positive, or a faulty sensor. EGR flow, hose and cooler checks are then suspended; MIL after two trips.

causes.label: Sensor ground open
Signal shorted to 5 V or positive
Sensor faulty internally
Engine module

symptoms: EGR readiness not set, EGR possibly switched off

P044E.title: EGR Sensor C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P044E.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor C is depends on the maker: on Ford petrol engines from 2020 it is the DPFE sensor, which measures the pressure drop across an orifice in the EGR pipe (sensor A there is the valve position sensor); GM diesels assign it to the position sensor of a low-pressure EGR valve, but only within fault groups. P044E means short dropouts or jumps in its signal, too brief for P044C/P044D or with an impossible rate of change. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; Ford applies the same idea to sensor A as P046D, where a limit violation of only 0.4 s counts. EGR diagnosis is then suspended.

causes.label: Loose contact in the connector or broken wire
Condensate in the sensor or hose (DPFE)
Sensor unstable internally
Interference or ground problems

symptoms: Check engine light on, may come and go

P044F.title: AIR System Switching Valve A Circuit High
P044F.description: After a cold start the secondary air pump blows fresh air into the exhaust; switching valve A is the electrically driven valve that opens this path. GM checks the valve circuit in three codes – P0412 open, P041F shorted to ground, P044F shorted to positive – while other makers use P0413/P0414 or P0412 for everything. P044F means the control circuit is shorted to positive or the coil is low-resistance: when the driver switches on, the line stays high. GM sets the code at 0.5 Ω or less to the supply (20 of 25 samples of 250 ms, above 11 V, MIL after two trips). The valve then does not open, secondary air is missing and P0411 may follow.

causes.label: Valve coil shorted internally (low resistance)
Control wire chafed against a supply wire
Water in the connector bridging to the supply
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Check engine light on (after two trips)
Secondary air readiness not set, possibly P0411

P0450.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
P0450.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The tank pressure sensor measures small pressures around ambient for the leak tests. Its direction differs by maker – on GM vacuum raises the voltage, on Ford and Bosch pressure does – so low and high refer to the signal voltage only. P0450 is the general circuit fault of tank pressure sensor A; makers that separate the fault use P0452 or P0453. Only Audi (2022/23) is documented with the code, as an electrical fault of the tank ventilation pressure sensor; GM, Ford and Saab do not use it. The leak tests are then suspended.

causes.label: Connector at the tank pressure sensor corroded or loose (underbody, splash water)
Tank pressure sensor faulty
Damaged 5 V, ground or signal wire
Engine module software

symptoms: EVAP readiness not set, emission inspection not passed

P0451.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Range/Performance
P0451.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The tank pressure sensor measures small pressures around ambient for the leak tests. Its direction differs by maker – on GM vacuum raises the voltage, on Ford and Bosch pressure does – so low and high refer to the signal voltage only. P0451 is its plausibility check. GM checks during the engine-off leak test that the signal settles to ambient pressure with the vent open and averages several tests; Ford checks the offset after at least 4–6 hours off (±0.5 kPa). Saab's Bosch ME9 watches start pressure, the drop during purging and excessive oscillation. On Subaru a leaking or blocked hose between sensor and tank is a frequent cause.

causes.label: Tank pressure sensor offset shifted or sluggish
Vent line or canister blocked (pressure does not release)
Sensor hose or port leaking, kinked or blocked
Tank overfilled, fuel in the lines

symptoms: EVAP readiness not set, emission inspection not passed

P0452.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Low
P0452.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The tank pressure sensor measures small pressures around ambient for the leak tests. Its direction differs by maker – on GM vacuum raises the voltage, on Ford and Bosch pressure does – so low and high refer to the signal voltage only. P0452 means its signal voltage is below the lower limit: GM below 0.15 V (640 of 800 samples, MIL after two trips), Ford below 0.1 V for 5 s, Saab below 0.1 V for more than 5 s. Common causes are a signal wire shorted to ground, an interrupted or shorted 5 V reference or a faulty sensor. Leak and purge tests are then suspended.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground or connector corroded
Tank pressure sensor faulty internally
5 V reference open or shorted (shared reference)
Engine module

symptoms: EVAP readiness not set, emission inspection not passed

P0453.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit High
P0453.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The tank pressure sensor measures small pressures around ambient for the leak tests. Its direction differs by maker – on GM vacuum raises the voltage, on Ford and Bosch pressure does – so low and high refer to the signal voltage only. P0453 means its signal voltage is above the upper limit: GM above 4.85 V (640 of 800 samples, MIL after two trips), Ford and Saab 9-4X above 4.9 V for 5 s. Ford states explicitly that an open circuit sets P0453, because the module's pull-up then drives the signal high. Other causes are a short to 5 V or battery voltage. Leak tests are then suspended.

causes.label: Signal or ground wire open, connector off
Tank pressure sensor faulty
Signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Engine module

symptoms: EVAP readiness not set, emission inspection not passed

P0454.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Intermittent
P0454.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The tank pressure sensor measures small pressures around ambient for the leak tests. Its direction differs by maker – on GM vacuum raises the voltage, on Ford and Bosch pressure does – so low and high refer to the signal voltage only. P0454 means the signal jumps. Ford checks continuously for a jump above about 1 kPa between two samples 100 ms apart or a brief open or short. GM (and the Saab 9-4X) checks only during the engine-off leak test: a jump of about 112 Pa within 1 s that refuelling cannot explain, 2 of 3 tests, MIL on the first trip. Saab's ME9 does not use the code. The engine-off small-leak test is then discarded.

causes.label: Loose contact at the connector to the tank pressure sensor
Chafed harness at the tank
Sensor faulty internally (noisy signal)
Fuel sloshing in an overfilled tank or refuelling misdetected

symptoms: EVAP readiness not set, emission inspection not passed

P0455.title: EVAP System Leak Detected - Large Leak
P0455.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0455 means a large leak or that no vacuum builds up. Ford pulls the closed system down with engine vacuum and expects about −2 kPa within 30 s; after refuelling it sets P0457 instead. GM sets the code if 20 litres have been purged without reaching 2740 Pa tank vacuum (once per cold start, MIL after two trips). Saab's ME9 uses a pressure drop below 525 Pa. The code also covers blocked purging, for example a purge valve stuck closed.

causes.label: Fuel cap missing, not clicked in or seal faulty (or capless flap)
Hose off or cracked (canister, filler neck, purge line)
Vent valve stuck open or purge valve stuck closed
Canister or filler neck cracked or corroded

symptoms: Check engine light on (possibly a check fuel cap message)
EVAP readiness or emission inspection not passed

P0456.title: EVAP System Leak Detected (very small leak)
P0456.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0456 reports a very small leak of 0.020 in (0.5 mm), as CARB requires. Ford uses the engine-off natural vacuum test: after switch-off the closed system must build at least about 190 Pa pressure or 125 Pa vacuum, judged statistically. Saab's Bosch ME9 also tests with the engine off for up to 45 minutes; VW and Audi use a leak detection pump. GM reports this leak size as P0442 instead. The code often appears only after many trips and depends on the weather.

causes.label: Fuel cap seal worn or cap not clicked in
Purge or vent valve not sealing
Porous hoses or O-rings, hairline crack in canister or filler neck
Leak detection pump itself leaking (VW/Audi)

symptoms: Check engine light on (possibly a check fuel cap message)
EVAP readiness or emission inspection not passed

P0457.title: EVAP System Leak Detected (fuel cap loose/off)
P0457.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0457 is a large leak attributed to the fuel cap: Ford detects refuelling and treats a vacuum that is not reached afterwards (about −2 kPa in 30 s) as an open cap. CARB allows a separate check fuel cap lamp instead of the warning lamp, and the code is cleared once the cap is found tight again. Ford sets the lamp after two to three trips depending on calibration, Subaru after two. GM and Saab's ME9 do not use the code.

causes.label: Fuel cap not closed, not clicked in or forgotten
Fuel cap seal faulty or non-original cap
Filler neck sealing surface damaged or capless flap sticking
Vent valve stuck open

symptoms: Check fuel cap lamp or check engine light on

P0458.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit Low
P0458.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Purge valve A is switched to ground by the module and fed from the main relay. P0458 means its control wire is shorted to ground: GM detects it with the driver off, when the line sits at ground instead of supply (20 of 25 samples, MIL after two trips); Saab's ME9 uses below 2.6 V at the output. The valve is then energised and open all the time, purging is uncontrolled – rough idle, rich mixture or hard starting after refuelling are possible.

causes.label: Purge valve control wire chafed against ground
Purge valve coil shorted internally
Connector scorched or wet
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Rough idle or rich mixture possible (valve permanently open)

P0459.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit High
P0459.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Purge valve A is switched to ground by the module and fed from the main relay. P0459 means its control wire is shorted to positive, detected with the driver switched on, when the line should sit at ground (GM 20 of 25 samples, MIL after two trips; Saab ME9 above 4.6 V). The valve then cannot open, the canister is not purged and fills up; the driver protects itself and the leak tests are suspended.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to battery voltage or supply
Purge valve coil low-resistance (shorted turns)
Connector or harness damaged
Engine module

symptoms: Fuel smell when the canister is full

P045A.title: EGR B Control Circuit
P045A.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR B is a second EGR valve next to valve A – on diesels with two EGR circuits the low-pressure valve, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor. GM's diesels of 2016–18 and FCA's 2.2-litre diesel in the Jeep Wrangler use it. P045A is the general electrical fault in the drive circuit of valve B, typically an open circuit (for valve A GM uses 200 kΩ or more). GM lists this code among those that switch off the low-pressure EGR position control, but publishes no thresholds for it; the description follows the comparable valve A checks and CARB, which requires output circuits to be monitored. Low-pressure EGR is then switched off.

causes.label: Connector at EGR valve B corroded or loose
Harness chafed or heat-damaged
Actuator motor in valve B open
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Low-pressure EGR switched off, possibly higher NOx

P045B.title: EGR B Control Circuit Range/Performance
P045B.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR B is a second EGR valve next to valve A – on diesels with two EGR circuits the low-pressure valve, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor. GM's diesels of 2016–18 and FCA's 2.2-litre diesel in the Jeep Wrangler use it. P045B means the drive circuit of valve B is electrically valid, but the feedback – current, voltage or position response – does not match the command. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows the valve A counterpart P0404 and CARB, which requires output functions to be checked where feasible. Typical is a coked, stiff valve.

causes.label: Valve B coked or stiff
Contact resistance in connector or wiring
Actuator motor worn internally
Engine module software or calibration

symptoms: Low-pressure EGR switched off, possibly higher NOx

P045C.title: EGR B Control Circuit Low
P045C.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR B is a second EGR valve next to valve A – on diesels with two EGR circuits the low-pressure valve, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor. GM's diesels of 2016–18 and FCA's 2.2-litre diesel in the Jeep Wrangler use it. P045C means the drive circuit of valve B is shorted to ground (for valve A, P0489, GM uses 0.5 Ω or less with the driver off, MIL after two trips). The driver is switched off for protection and the valve stays in its rest position. GM lists this code among those that switch off the low-pressure EGR position control, but publishes no thresholds for it; the description follows the comparable valve A checks and CARB, which requires output circuits to be monitored.

causes.label: Control wire chafed against ground (engine, exhaust)
Actuator motor winding shorted
Water or corrosion in the connector
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Low-pressure EGR switched off, possibly higher NOx

P045D.title: EGR B Control Circuit High
P045D.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR B is a second EGR valve next to valve A – on diesels with two EGR circuits the low-pressure valve, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor. GM's diesels of 2016–18 and FCA's 2.2-litre diesel in the Jeep Wrangler use it. P045D means the drive circuit of valve B is shorted to the supply, or the actuator draws overcurrent with the driver on (comparable to P0490 for valve A). The driver is switched off and EGR B stays inactive. GM lists this code among those that switch off the low-pressure EGR position control, but publishes no thresholds for it; the description follows the comparable valve A checks and CARB, which requires output circuits to be monitored.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a supply wire
Actuator motor shorted internally (overcurrent)
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Engine module

symptoms: Low-pressure EGR switched off, possibly higher NOx

P045E.title: EGR B Control Stuck Open
P045E.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR B is a second EGR valve next to valve A – on diesels with two EGR circuits the low-pressure valve, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor. GM's diesels of 2016–18 and FCA's 2.2-litre diesel in the Jeep Wrangler use it. P045E means valve B does not close: its actual position stays above the target despite the close command. On FCA's 2.2-litre diesel in the Jeep Wrangler, deposits in the low-pressure valve cause it; the bulletin prescribes a cleaning routine of nine ignition cycles that moves the valve repeatedly. Another FCA bulletin shows P045E following a position sensor fault (P0407/P0408). Too much EGR causes misfire, lack of power and smoke.

causes.label: Soot or condensate deposits in the low-pressure valve
Valve position sensor fault as the trigger
Actuator gear or return spring faulty
Foreign matter or filter debris in the low-pressure circuit

symptoms: Lack of power, rough running, misfire

P045F.title: EGR B Control Stuck Closed
P045F.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR B is a second EGR valve next to valve A – on diesels with two EGR circuits the low-pressure valve, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor. GM's diesels of 2016–18 and FCA's 2.2-litre diesel in the Jeep Wrangler use it. P045F means valve B does not open: its actual position stays below the target despite the open command. GM lists the code among those that switch off low-pressure EGR control; Ford's comparable valve A check (P042F) compares the position with a calculated lower limit. causes.label: Low-pressure valve coked or stuck
Actuator motor or gear faulty
Icing or condensate in the low-pressure circuit
Position sensor reports a wrong position

symptoms: Low-pressure EGR switched off, possibly higher NOx

P0460.title: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit
P0460.description: The fuel level sensor is a float on a resistor track in the tank unit. It is no emission part, but other monitors depend on it – the EVAP leak tests, for example, need at least 15 % fuel – so CARB requires it to be monitored and the usual exemption from the warning lamp does not apply. P0460 is the general circuit code for sensor A, the main or only fuel level sensor. Ford sets it instead of P0462/P0463 below 5 Ω or above 200 Ω for 30 s and until about 2012 also used it for a stuck sensor (fuel use compared over 100–120 miles); Saab's Trionic T8 uses it for a sensor that does not change. GM does not use P0460. The gauge then shows wrong values or a substitute, and level-dependent monitors do not run.

causes.label: Resistor track worn or float arm sticking
Wire or connector at the tank unit open or shorted (corrosion)
Instrument cluster or gateway sends a wrong value (if the level comes via the bus)
Frequent topping up or overfilling (plausibility test fails without a defect)

symptoms: Fuel gauge wrong, stuck or jumping
Range display and low-fuel warning wrong
Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0462.title: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Low
P0462.description: The fuel level sensor is a float on a resistor track in the tank unit. P0465.title: EVAP Purge Flow Sensor Circuit
P0465.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. A purge flow sensor – a heated thermistor in the purge line between purge valve and intake manifold, as described in a Ford patent – measures purge flow directly for the CARB purge monitor. Today indirect methods (fuel trim, tank vacuum) have largely replaced it; no manufacturer document available to us uses these codes. P0465 is the general circuit fault of the sensor (heater supply, signal or ground), which CARB requires to be checked continuously. The purge flow monitor can then not be evaluated.

causes.label: Connector or wire at the purge flow sensor
Sensor (heater or thermistor) faulty
Engine module

symptoms: EVAP readiness not set, emission inspection not passed

P046A.title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation Bank 1
P046A.description: Some engines measure the catalyst temperature with sensors instead of only modelling it. P046A compares catalyst temperature sensors 1 and 2 of bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1): both are electrically valid, but their readings do not match – for example they differ after a long stop, or the difference does not fit the operating state. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; FCA's EcoDiesel has only one such sensor per bank, and most makers handle exhaust temperature sensors and their correlation under EGT codes such as P0544 ff or P24C2. The description follows CARB's plausibility requirement for input components.

causes.label: One of the two sensors drifting (soot on the tip, ageing)
Sensors fitted or connected the wrong way round
Contact resistance at one sensor's connector
Exhaust leak between the sensors

P046C.title: EGR Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P046C.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Which part EGR sensors A and B are depends on the maker: sensor A is usually the position sensor of EGR valve A; GM's Duramax diesels of 2017/18 use sensor B for the coolant temperature sensor at the inlet of the high-pressure EGR cooler, FCA for the position sensor of the low-pressure valve. P046C means the signal of sensor A is electrically valid but implausible. GM's diesels (6.6-litre Duramax LML and others from 2014) set it when the actual valve position deviates from the target by 5 % or more for 8 s, with offset learning completed and at least 11 V (MIL after two trips). Ford uses P0405/P0406/P046D for sensor A instead. EGR is then switched off or limited.

Position sensor worn or offset shifted
Contact resistance at connector or 5 V supply
Values not relearned after valve replacement

symptoms: EGR switched off, possibly higher NOx
Rarely jerking or lack of power

P046D.title: EGR Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

Disturbed 5 V reference

Occasional jerking when EGR switches off

P046E.title: EGR Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P046E.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Sensor faulty internally
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light on, may come and go

P0470.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P0470.description: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure. P0470 is the general circuit fault of sensor A. Ford's 6.7-litre diesel with a digital SENT sensor sets it when the sensor reports an error status or its raw data leave their limits for 5 s; a loss of communication is U0691 instead. Analogue sensors use it for an open or unspecified circuit fault where low and high are not separated.

causes.label: Sensor faulty internally
Connector corroded or heat-damaged near the manifold
Broken or chafed signal or 5 V wire
Engine module or software

symptoms: EGR and turbo control on a substitute value, possibly reduced power
Exhaust brake or warm-up flap without function

P0471.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0471.description: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). Real high back pressure from a clogged particulate filter or catalyst
Leaking sensing tube or exhaust leak ahead of the sensor

Exhaust brake or warm-up flap without function

P0475.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A
P0475.description: The exhaust pressure control valve is a flap in the exhaust: on older Navistar/Ford diesels a warm-up flap that raises back pressure when cold, on Ram and others an exhaust brake, on VW's 2.0 TDI a flap that drives the low-pressure EGR, and on Audi and Bentley a sound flap. Wire or connector at the exhaust damaged or corroded
Control wire open
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Flap without function: sound unchanged, rattling
Diesel: longer warm-up, exhaust brake weak or EGR faults

P0476.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Range/Performance
P0476.description: The exhaust pressure control valve is a flap in the exhaust: on older Navistar/Ford diesels a warm-up flap that raises back pressure when cold, on Ram and others an exhaust brake, on VW's 2.0 TDI a flap that drives the low-pressure EGR, and on Audi and Bentley a sound flap.
