P047E.description: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure. No manufacturer document available to us uses sensor B – it would be a second sensor, for example on bank 2 of a twin-turbo engine; the description mirrors sensor A. P047E means the signal of sensor B jumps or deviates from the model in operation (for sensor A Ford uses more than 500 kPa or below −100 kPa for 2 s).

causes.label: Loose contact at connector or wire near the hot manifold
Sensing tube partly blocked (sluggish, jumping values)
Engine module software (Ford 6.7, 2018)
Sensor faulty

symptoms: EGR and turbo control on a substitute value, possibly reduced power
Exhaust brake or warm-up flap without function

P047F.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Stuck Open
P047F.description: The exhaust pressure control valve is a flap in the exhaust: on older Navistar/Ford diesels a warm-up flap that raises back pressure when cold, on Ram and others an exhaust brake, on VW's 2.0 TDI a flap that drives the low-pressure EGR, and on Audi and Bentley a sound flap. P047F means valve A stays open although it is commanded to close, detected by the flap's position sensor or by missing back pressure. On VW's 2.0 TDI and Audi's A3 TDI of 2009–12 the code appears with P0477, P048A–P048C and P0401: water and road salt corrode the flap shaft so the flap sticks; improved parts were introduced. As the flap drives the low-pressure EGR there, EGR flow is then too low.

causes.label: Flap shaft corroded or seized
Soot or carbon on the flap
Actuator or linkage faulty or unhooked
Position sensor reports wrongly

symptoms: EGR flow too low (P0401), higher NOx
Exhaust brake or warm-up flap without effect, possibly louder exhaust

P0480.title: Fan 1 Control Circuit
P0480.description: The engine module switches the radiator fan either through a relay, whose coil it pulls to ground, or with a PWM signal to a fan control module. The circuit is an output that CARB requires to be checked continuously. P0480 concerns the control circuit of fan 1. GM sets it for an open circuit – 200 kΩ or more with the driver off, 50 of 63 samples, above 11 V, MIL after two trips – and reports a short to ground or positive as P0691/P0692; Saab models on GM technology set it after 5 s (relay) or 1 s (PWM). FCA bulletins also name it with the warning lamp. Ford's OBD summaries do not contain the code. If the fan stops, the engine can overheat in traffic and the air conditioning weakens at standstill.

causes.label: Fan relay (coil open) or fan control module faulty
Connector at fan or relay corroded, water ingress or pin pushed out
Control wire open or shorted to ground
Fan motor or fan assembly faulty
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Radiator fan does not run, or runs constantly
Overheating at standstill or in traffic

P0481.title: Fan 2 Control Circuit
P0481.description: The engine module switches the radiator fan either through a relay, whose coil it pulls to ground, or with a PWM signal to a fan control module. The circuit is an output that CARB requires to be checked continuously. P0481 concerns the second fan control circuit – depending on the design a second fan or a second speed stage; on GM and Saab, relays 2 and 3 switch the fans in series or parallel for low and high speed. GM sets it for an open circuit (200 kΩ or more, 50 of 63 samples, MIL after two trips) and reports shorts as P0693/P0694. Ford's OBD summaries do not contain the code. One fan stage then fails or runs constantly; cooling usually remains partly available.

causes.label: Fan relay 2 (or 2/3) faulty
Corrosion or water in relay or fan connector
Control wire open or shorted to ground
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: One fan stage or fan not working, or running constantly

P0482.title: Fan 3 Control Circuit
P0482.description: The engine module switches cooling fan stages through relays, pulling each relay coil to ground. P0482 concerns the control circuit of the third stage or relay: with the driver off the line should sit at battery voltage through the coil, and the internal pull-up level means an open circuit (Saab ME9: more than 1 s, 10–18 V, engine running). On the GM-based Saab 9-5 of 2011 it is relay 3 (medium stage) of a two-fan network, with shorts reported as P0695/P0696. GM tables list P0482 only in fault groups; Ford's OBD summaries do not contain it. One fan stage then fails.

causes.label: Fan relay 3 faulty (coil open) or not seated properly
Control wire open or high-resistance, corroded or backed-out pins
Relay coil supply missing (fuse, supply wire)
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: One fan stage fails – temperature rises in traffic or when towing

P0483.title: Fan Rationality Check
P0483.description: Two kinds of cooling fan carry these codes: electric fans switched by relays or driven by a PWM/LIN fan module with speed feedback, and engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch, whose speed a Hall sensor reports – GM calls them EV fans, meaning electro-viscous, not electric vehicle. P0483 checks the fan's function, not its circuit. With a speed sensor (GM viscous fans) commanded and actual speed are compared: GM's Duramax diesels of 2014–18 set it at more than ±500 rpm for at least 120 s, GM petrol SUVs and pick-ups of 2004–06 at more than 1000 rpm – MIL after two trips. Without a sensor Subaru (and the Saab 9-2X) judges indirectly: if coolant at 100 °C or more does not fall within 5 minutes at idle with the fan on, the code sets after two trips. Ford's OBD summaries do not contain it.

causes.label: Viscous clutch worn or leaking, or its solenoid faulty – fan does not reach or leave target speed
Electric fan motor stiff or worn, or fan blocked
Fan speed sensor or wiring giving a wrong value
Radiator or condenser clogged, coolant low (Subaru logic)
Drive belt slipping (belt-driven viscous fan)

symptoms: Check engine light on (after two trips)
Constant fan roar, or temperature rise at standstill
Air conditioning weak at low speed

P0484.title: Fan Circuit Current High
P0484.description: P0484 monitors the current drawn in the fan's load circuit: if it exceeds a threshold – blocked or stiff motor, shorted turns, a short in the load circuit – the code sets. This is only possible where the fan runs on a current-measuring semiconductor driver or fan module; plain relay circuits do not measure load current. Supplier patents (Bosch and others) describe current limiting or switch-off after a few seconds of overcurrent, ignoring the inrush current. No manufacturer table available to us lists P0484, so thresholds and warning-lamp behaviour remain open; CARB requires output components to be monitored.

causes.label: Fan motor stiff (bearing damage) or blocked (foreign object, ice, bent blade)
Shorted turns or worn brushes in the fan motor
Short in the load circuit (pinched or chafed wire)
Fan control module faulty (wrong current measurement)

symptoms: Fan does not run, runs only briefly or at reduced power
Humming or grinding at the fan, possibly blown fan fuse

P0485.title: Fan Power/Ground Circuit
P0485.description: P0485 monitors the supply or ground path of the fan or its control module – not the control line. It is typical of fans with their own module (PWM or LIN), which can report undervoltage or a missing ground. The high currents involved, often 20–60 A, make contact resistance at ground and supply connections and fuse holders the main cause. No manufacturer table available to us lists P0485, so thresholds and warning-lamp behaviour remain open; CARB requires output components to be monitored. The fan then runs intermittently or not at all.

causes.label: Fan or fan module ground loose, corroded or broken
Fan fuse blown or fuse holder overheated or corroded
Relay power contact burnt – voltage drop under load
Connector at the fan scorched, water ingress
Fan control module faulty

symptoms: Fan does not run or only intermittently
Overheating at standstill, weak air conditioning
Possibly burnt smell or discoloured connector

P0486.title: EGR Sensor B Circuit
P0486.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Which part EGR sensor B is depends on the maker: FCA uses it for the position sensor of the low-pressure EGR valve, GM's Duramax diesels for the coolant temperature sensor at the EGR cooler inlet. P0486 is its general circuit fault without a low or high assignment. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – makers report sensor B as P0407/P0408, P046E and P046F – so the description follows CARB's input component rules. EGR is then switched off or uses a substitute value.

causes.label: Connector or harness to sensor B corroded or open (heat at the exhaust)
Sensor B faulty
5 V reference or ground disturbed
Engine module or software

symptoms: EGR switched off, usually no noticeable change

P0487.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A/Open
P0487.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. The EGR throttle is a regulating flap ahead of the intake manifold on diesels: by closing partly it lowers manifold pressure below exhaust back pressure so that enough exhaust is recirculated, and it also helps filter regeneration and shuts off air at engine stop. It is usually a DC motor with position sensor. GM and Ford report this flap under P02E0 ff; no manufacturer document available to us uses this code. P0487 means its drive circuit is open or has a general circuit fault, detected by the output stage. The flap then stays open, so the EGR rate cannot be raised enough and filter regeneration may be blocked.

causes.label: Connector at the flap corroded or loose, wire open
Flap actuator motor faulty (winding open)
Pneumatic version: vacuum converter faulty
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode possible
Shaking when the engine is switched off

P0488.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A Range/Performance
P0488.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. The EGR throttle is a regulating flap ahead of the intake manifold on diesels: by closing partly it lowers manifold pressure below exhaust back pressure so that enough exhaust is recirculated, and it also helps filter regeneration and shuts off air at engine stop. It is usually a DC motor with position sensor. GM and Ford report this flap under P02E0 ff; no manufacturer document available to us uses this code. P0488 is its function check: the actual position reported by the sensor deviates from the target for too long, or the position signal is implausible – typically a coked, stiff flap or a broken gear. The flap then goes to its rest position or the engine enters limp mode, and the EGR rate cannot be controlled.

causes.label: Flap coked by soot and oil mist (EGR plus crankcase ventilation)
Actuator gear or motor worn or broken
Position sensor in the flap faulty or implausible
Corrosion on flap or housing

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode possible
Shaking when the engine is switched off

P0489.title: EGR A Control Circuit Low
P0489.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0489 means the drive circuit of EGR valve A – solenoid, stepper or DC motor – is shorted to ground. GM's Duramax LML sets it at 0.5 Ω or less to ground for 3 s, GM's 2016 diesels after 96 of 120 samples, Ford diesels after 0.35 s, Saab's 2.0 TiD likewise – MIL after two trips. The valve is usually switched off; with low-side control a short to ground can keep it energised and open, causing rough idle or stalling.

causes.label: Harness chafed at the exhaust with short to ground
EGR valve winding shorted to its housing
Water or corrosion in the connector
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Rough idle or stalling if the valve stays open

P048A.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Stuck Closed
P048A.description: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2. Documented uses are the flap behind the particulate filter of VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI, which raises back pressure for the low-pressure EGR, and the sound flaps of Audi and Bentley. P048A means valve A is commanded open but its position feedback stays closed. On VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI of 2009–13 water and road salt corrode the shaft of the low-pressure EGR flap so it sticks; the code appears with P047F, P0477, P048B/P048C and P0401. The bulletins advise removing the flap and checking it moves freely, otherwise replacing it; improved parts were introduced. A closed flap keeps back pressure high.

causes.label: Flap or flap shaft corroded or coked (stiff)
Flap actuator (motor or gear) faulty or too weak
Linkage between actuator and flap broken or misadjusted
Position sensor reports wrongly

symptoms: Flap without function, exhaust sound changed
VW/Audi TDI: EGR fault P0401 possible

P048B.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit
P048B.description: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2. Documented uses are the flap behind the particulate filter of VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI, which raises back pressure for the low-pressure EGR, and the sound flaps of Audi and Bentley. P048B is the general circuit fault or open circuit of valve A's position sensor or end switch. VW's 2.0 TDI of 2009–13 sets it with a corroded flap; on the 2015 engine it appears with P048E, P0475, P0477 and P0478 and the actuator with its integrated electronics is replaced; Bentley's V8 of 2023 reports it for bank 1 together with P048D. As the sensor sits in the actuator, a circuit fault often means actuator electronics.

causes.label: Actuator with integrated position sensor faulty
Connector or wire at the underbody corroded, chafed or open
Engine module (sensor supply or input)

symptoms: Flap without function, exhaust sound changed
VW/Audi TDI: EGR fault P0401 possible

P048C.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P048C.description: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2. Documented uses are the flap behind the particulate filter of VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI, which raises back pressure for the low-pressure EGR, and the sound flaps of Audi and Bentley. P048C means valve A's position signal is electrically valid but does not match the commanded position or the learned end positions. It is documented only on VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI of 2009–13, together with P047F, P048A, P048B and P0401, caused by the corroded, sticking flap shaft. After replacing the actuator, the end positions must be relearned.

causes.label: Flap or shaft corroded or coked (stiff)
End positions not relearned after replacement
Position sensor in the actuator drifting
Contact resistance in the connector

symptoms: Flap without function, exhaust sound changed
VW/Audi TDI: EGR fault P0401 possible

P048D.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P048D.description: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2. Documented uses are the flap behind the particulate filter of VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI, which raises back pressure for the low-pressure EGR, and the sound flaps of Audi and Bentley. P048D means valve A's position signal is below its permitted voltage window – the signal wire is shorted to ground or the sensor's 5 V supply is missing. Bentley's Continental and Flying Spur V8 of 2023 report it for bank 1 together with P048B; the bulletin advises checking wiring and contacts, otherwise replacing the actuator and carrying out the basic setting.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground (chafed at the underbody)
Position sensor or actuator faulty internally
5 V sensor supply open or shorted
Moisture or corrosion in the connector

symptoms: Flap without function, exhaust sound changed
VW/Audi TDI: EGR fault P0401 possible

P048E.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P048E.description: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2. Documented uses are the flap behind the particulate filter of VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI, which raises back pressure for the low-pressure EGR, and the sound flaps of Audi and Bentley. P048E means valve A's position signal is above its window – an open signal pulled up, or a short to positive. VW's 2.0 TDI third generation of 2015 sets it together with P048B, P0475, P0477 and P0478: the flap is welded into the pipe, so with electronic faults only the actuator is replaced – an electrostatic-sensitive part that must be scrapped if dropped.

causes.label: Actuator electronics (position sensor) faulty
Signal or ground wire open
Connector corroded
Signal shorted to positive

symptoms: Flap without function, exhaust sound changed
VW/Audi TDI: EGR fault P0401 possible

P048F.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P048F.description: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2. Documented uses are the flap behind the particulate filter of VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI, which raises back pressure for the low-pressure EGR, and the sound flaps of Audi and Bentley. P048F means valve A's position signal jumps, drops out briefly or changes faster than physically possible. Bentley stores sporadic sensor faults under the low code with a sporadic status instead. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows the sibling codes P048B–P048E and CARB.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the actuator connector
Wire broken by vibration or heat
Position sensor worn

symptoms: Flap without function, exhaust sound changed
VW/Audi TDI: EGR fault P0401 possible

P0490.title: EGR A Control Circuit High
P0490.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0490 means the drive circuit of EGR valve A is shorted to battery voltage, or its output stage sees overcurrent. GM's Duramax LML sets it at 0.5 Ω or less to the supply for 3 s, GM's 2017 diesels at an H-bridge current above 8 A (160 of 200 samples), Ford diesels after 0.35 s – MIL after two trips. The output stage switches off for protection and the valve falls into its spring position, closed; EGR is off.

causes.label: Harness shorted to a supply wire (chafing)
EGR valve with shorted turns (low resistance, overcurrent)
Moisture in the connector
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: EGR switched off, usually no noticeable change

P0491.title: AIR System Insufficient Flow Bank 1
P0491.description: After a cold start the secondary air pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; CARB requires the air flow to be monitored per bank. P0491 means too little air reaches bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1). VW and Audi calculate the injected air mass per bank from the front oxygen sensor's reaction during the cold-start phase; an Audi bulletin names values of 0.4–0.7 on both banks as too little together, often from coked air passages in the cylinder head. On VW/Audi V engines each bank has its own combination valve with a shared pump. Ford assigns the code to the bank 1 secondary air monitor; GM uses P0411 instead.

causes.label: Secondary air passages in the cylinder head coked
Combination valve stuck or stiff
Vacuum supply or changeover valve leaking, valve closes too early
Secondary air pump weak or water in the pump
Hose between pump and valve leaking or off

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)
Possibly no pump noise after a cold start

P0492.title: AIR System Insufficient Flow Bank 2
P0492.description: After a cold start the secondary air pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; CARB requires the air flow to be monitored per bank. P0492 means too little air reaches bank 2 (the side without cylinder 1). VW and Audi calculate the injected air mass per bank from the front oxygen sensor's reaction during the cold-start phase; an Audi bulletin names values of 0.4–0.7 on both banks as too little together, often from coked air passages in the cylinder head. On VW/Audi V engines each bank has its own combination valve with a shared pump. Ford assigns the code to the bank 2 secondary air monitor; GM uses P0411 instead.

causes.label: Secondary air passages in the cylinder head coked
Combination valve stuck or stiff
Vacuum supply or changeover valve leaking, valve closes too early
Secondary air pump weak or water in the pump
Hose between pump and valve leaking or off

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)
Possibly no pump noise after a cold start

P0493.title: Fan Overspeed
P0493.description: Two kinds of cooling fan carry these codes: electric fans switched by relays or driven by a PWM/LIN fan module with speed feedback, and engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch, whose speed a Hall sensor reports – GM calls them EV fans, meaning electro-viscous, not electric vehicle. P0493 is documented only on GM petrol engines of 2004–06 with a viscous fan: the measured fan speed exceeds a limit that is hardly physically possible (about 6400 rpm), so it is effectively a plausibility check of the speed signal or a seized clutch at high engine speed. Two counts set it, with the warning lamp on the first trip – unlike P0495, which needs two trips. Ford, FCA and GM from 2014 were not found to use it.

causes.label: Viscous clutch seized – fan runs rigidly with the belt drive
Interference or faulty signal from the fan speed sensor
Clutch solenoid or its control stuck at fully engaged
Engine module or software

symptoms: Loud fan roar at higher revs

P0494.title: Fan 1 Underspeed
P0494.description: Two kinds of cooling fan carry these codes: electric fans switched by relays or driven by a PWM/LIN fan module with speed feedback, and engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch, whose speed a Hall sensor reports – GM calls them EV fans, meaning electro-viscous, not electric vehicle. P0494 means fan 1 turns slower than commanded, judged from the speed reported by a LIN fan module or the clutch's speed sensor. GM's 2.0-litre turbo of 2020 uses a lower limit of about 59 % of the target at 750 rpm, rising to about 76 % at 2750 rpm and above. GM bulletins name an internal fan fault on the Equinox/Terrain 1.5 and water slowing the fan on the Hummer EV; Ford's 6.7-litre Super Duty uses it for the viscous fan and warns against replacing the clutch too quickly.

causes.label: Fan motor or fan module faulty or worn (brushes, bearings, electronics)
Fan slowed or blocked (water, snow, ice, foreign object, distorted shroud)
Viscous clutch slipping or low on fluid, clutch valve faulty
High-resistance supply or ground, connector problems
Faulty speed signal (sensor or LIN feedback)

symptoms: Check engine light on (depending on the maker)
Temperature rises at standstill or when towing

P0495.title: Fan 1 Overspeed
P0495.description: Two kinds of cooling fan carry these codes: electric fans switched by relays or driven by a PWM/LIN fan module with speed feedback, and engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch, whose speed a Hall sensor reports – GM calls them EV fans, meaning electro-viscous, not electric vehicle. P0495 mainly concerns viscous fans: with the fan commanded off it turns faster than the permitted drag speed, so the clutch does not release. GM thresholds: Duramax 2016 above 1500 rpm, Duramax 2018 above a calculated drag speed, petrol SUVs of 2004–05 above 1600 rpm without command – all with the warning lamp after two trips; Ford's 6.7-litre Super Duty uses it the same way. On GM's 2020 2.0-litre turbo with a LIN electric fan it means a reported speed above 2900 rpm.

causes.label: Viscous clutch does not release (gummed, overfilled, seized)
Clutch solenoid or its control stuck open (short to positive, valve sticking)
Wrong speed signal (sensor, wiring, interference)
Electric fan: module runs uncontrolled at full speed or relay sticking

symptoms: Loud fan roar even with a cold engine or at idle

P0496.title: EVAP System High Purge Flow
P0496.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0496 means vapour flows into the intake although the module is not purging – usually a purge valve that leaks or sticks open. GM and Saab seal the system after a cold start with the engine running; if tank vacuum exceeds 2491 Pa for 5 s, the code sets (fuel 10–90 %, MIL after two trips). Ford, which replaced its old code P1450 with P0496, also sets it for excessive vacuum during the leak test, for example with a vent valve stuck closed. Hard starting right after refuelling is typical.

causes.label: Purge valve leaking or stuck open (charcoal dust in the seat)
Vent valve stuck closed or vent filter or line blocked
Vapour line kinked or blocked
Tank pressure sensor reading wrong

symptoms: Hard or long starting right after refuelling
Hissing vacuum when opening the fuel cap

P0497.title: EVAP System Low Purge Flow
P0497.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0497 is the counterpart of P0496: the module purges but sees too little or no purge flow, judged indirectly from fuel trim, idle control or tank vacuum – CARB requires missing purge flow to be detected. Code-specific use is documented only by Land Rover (5.0-litre V8) and in a GM fault group for systems with a sealed tank (Volt, ELR); standard GM and Ford systems use other codes, such as P0455. The canister is then not purged and saturates.

causes.label: Purge valve stuck closed, does not open
Purge line off, kinked or blocked (check valve sticking)
Canister or vent filter blocked (e.g. after overfilling)
Vent valve stuck closed

P0498.title: EVAP System Vent Valve Control Circuit Low
P0498.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The vent valve is normally open and switched to ground by the module; P0449 (open), P0498 and P0499 form the newer code scheme for its circuit, used mainly by GM and Saab models with GM engines, while Ford uses P0446. P0498 means the control wire is shorted to ground: GM sees 0.5 Ω or less to ground with the driver off (20 of 25 samples), Saab below 2.6 V – MIL after two trips. The valve is then permanently energised and closed, so the tank is not vented and refuelling becomes difficult.

causes.label: Vent valve control wire chafed against ground (underbody, tank area)
Vent valve coil shorted internally
Corrosion or water in the connector
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Vacuum noise when opening the fuel cap

P0499.title: EVAP System Vent Valve Control Circuit High
P0499.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The vent valve is normally open and switched to ground by the module (GM scheme P0449/P0498/P0499; Ford uses P0446). P0499 means the control wire is shorted to positive: with the driver on the output stays high – GM sees 0.5 Ω or less to the supply, Saab above 4.6 V; MIL after two trips. The valve then cannot close, the system cannot be sealed, and the leak tests are suspended because they would otherwise report a large leak.

causes.label: Control wire touching battery positive or the valve supply (chafed harness)
Vent valve coil with shorted turns, driver switches off
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver in the engine module

P049A.title: EGR B Flow
P049A.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Circuit B is the second EGR path; on diesels with two circuits it is the low-pressure EGR, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor (GM diesels 2016–18, FCA's 2.2 and 3.0 diesels). P049A is the general flow fault of circuit B, used where the module does not separate too little from too much; CARB requires low and high flow to be detected, mostly by comparing air mass, manifold pressure or lambda with a model. No manufacturer document available to us uses P049A – GM has only position and actuator codes for its low-pressure EGR, FCA uses P049B. Low-pressure EGR is then switched off.

causes.label: Low-pressure EGR valve sooted or sticking
Low-pressure EGR cooler or line blocked or leaking
Flap creating the pressure difference faulty
Sensors (air mass, pressure difference, position sensor B) implausible

symptoms: EGR switched off, usually no noticeable change

P049B.title: EGR B Flow Insufficient Detected
P049B.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Circuit B is the second EGR path; on diesels with two circuits it is the low-pressure EGR, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor (GM diesels 2016–18, FCA's 2.2 and 3.0 diesels). P049B means too little flow in circuit B: with the low-pressure valve open the module expects a change in fresh air mass or manifold pressure, or a modelled EGR volume, and the actual flow stays below the threshold. FCA documents it on the 3.0-litre EcoDiesel third generation in the 2020 Ram 1500, partly as a false trigger fixed by a software update; thresholds are not published.

causes.label: Software or calibration (false trigger)
Low-pressure EGR valve sooted or stuck closed
Low-pressure EGR cooler or line blocked
Implausible sensors (air mass, pressure difference)

P049C.title: EGR B Flow Excessive Detected

P04AB.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Circuit/Open
P04AB.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Purge valve B is a second electric purge valve, usually for the high-load purge line of a turbo engine, which purges to the compressor inlet when there is boost in the manifold (Ford patent). Many makers solve this path with one purge valve and passive check valves instead – Ford tests it as P04F0 – and then have no valve B. CARB requires every purge path to be checked. P04AB means the control circuit of purge valve B is open; the high-load path then does not purge. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the comparable purge valve A checks (for GM P0443/P0458/P0459).

causes.label: Purge valve B connector loose or corroded

Supply (fuse, main relay) or control wire open
Driver in the engine module

P04B0.title: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Circuit/Open
P04B0.description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Plug-in hybrids and range extenders with a sealed, pressurised tank have an electric valve in the vapour line between tank and canister. It is normally closed and opens before refuelling, so that the tank is depressurised – the filler flap is only released then – and refuelling vapour reaches the canister (Ford patent). Supply or control wire open
Driver in the control module

P04B4.title: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Stuck Closed
P04B4.description: Plug-in and some full hybrids keep the fuel tank sealed while driving, separated from the charcoal canister by a valve. When the driver presses the fuel button, the system opens the valve, lets the pressure escape into the canister and only then unlocks the filler door. A switch reports whether the door is open or closed, so that the tank can be sealed again afterwards. P04B4 is the function check of the valve between tank and canister: after the open command the tank pressure must move towards canister or ambient pressure, and if the rate of change stays below a threshold the valve counts as stuck closed (Ford patent). The tank then cannot be depressurised, the door does not unlock or only after a long delay, and during refuelling vapour cannot reach the canister. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code.

Vapour line kinked or blocked, liquid separator blocked
Canister clogged (charcoal dust, liquid fuel)
Tank pressure sensor sluggish or wrong

P04B5.title: Fuel Fill Door Stuck Open

P04D7 means the signal changes state abruptly or too often, or shows brief excursions too short for the low/high codes – bouncing contacts or a loose connection.

causes.label: Loose contact at the button or module connector
Worn or bouncing button
Chafed wire with intermittent short
Moisture or corrosion

symptoms: Exhaust brake cannot be switched on, button lamp off or wrong
More load on the service brakes downhill

P04D8.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop EGR Control
P04D8.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Where EGR is closed-loop controlled – on flow, valve position or pressure difference – CARB requires the control to start within a time set by the maker after starting; otherwise a fault is due, and P04D8 is that code. Typical prerequisites are coolant or cooler temperature, valid sensors and an operating range; Ford diesels, for example, run their EGR monitors only with EGR in closed loop. No manufacturer document available to us uses P04D8 – many monitor the inputs individually instead, as CARB permits.

causes.label: Engine reaches release temperature too late (thermostat stuck open, very short trips, cold weather)
Faulty input sensor blocks the release (EGR temperature, air mass, position)
EGR valve or actuator not ready (stuck, learned value missing)
Software or calibration

symptoms: Often together with coolant or sensor codes

P04D9.title: Closed Loop EGR Control At Limit - Flow Too Low
P04D9.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P04D9 means the EGR control has used up its authority and still gets too little flow – CARB requires this to be detected. Ford's 6.7-litre diesel sets it when the desired minus the measured EGR rate stays above 50 points for 20 s. Volvo cars from 2022 also set it after long low-load driving and fix it with a software update and an activation drive; a Mack/Volvo truck bulletin traces it to wrong EGR temperature readings from worn connector contacts.

causes.label: EGR cooler, valve or pipes sooted or narrowed
EGR valve sticking or not opening fully
EGR rate mismeasured (temperature sensor contacts, air mass meter, pressure sensor)
Software or driving profile with long low-load operation

symptoms: Higher NOx, petrol engines may knock

P04DA.title: Closed Loop EGR Control At Limit - Flow Too High
P04DA.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P04DA is the counterpart of P04D9: the control cannot lower the flow far enough even at the end of its range. CARB requires this for petrol engines from model years 2019–21 and for diesels. Ford's 6.7-litre diesel sets it when the desired minus the measured EGR rate stays below −60 points for 20 s with EGR in closed loop. Too much exhaust in the cylinder causes soot, rough running and, on petrol engines, misfire up to stalling at idle.

causes.label: EGR valve not closing (soot at the seat, stuck open)
Air mass meter reading too little fresh air (EGR rate calculated too high)
Position or EGR temperature sensor giving a wrong value
Intake or exhaust throttle wrong (pressure difference too large)

symptoms: Smoke or soot (diesel), possibly stalling at idle (petrol)

P04DB.title: Crankcase Ventilation System Disconnected
P04DB.description: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) system routes blow-by gas from the crankcase into the intake; CARB requires a disconnection between crankcase and intake to be detected. GM's 2.0-litre LSY has a pressure sensor in the PCV hose: with the hose connected it must see a pressure drop that grows with air flow, plus pressure pulses from the pistons. Ford reports the same sensor type as crankcase pressure sensor A (P051A ff). P04DB means a disconnection: without the pressure drop the clean-air side is off, without the pulses the crankcase side. GM's LSY uses the product of normalised offset and noise (below 0.63 kPa², MIL after two trips); Ford's EcoBoost checks the dirty side at cranking and the clean side above 5 lb/min of air. Engines without such a sensor may report a disconnection through mixture or load codes, as CARB allows. FCA bulletins cover it on the Alfa Romeo 2.0 turbo and the Ram 3.0 EcoDiesel.

causes.label: Ventilation hose off or quick connector not latched (often after intake work)
Hose cracked or porous, or nipple broken
PCV valve stuck closed or oil separator blocked or frozen (simulates a disconnection)
Pressure sensor in the hose giving a wrong signal

symptoms: Hissing, false air, rough idle or lean running
Oil mist or smell in the engine bay

P04DC.title: Fuel Fill Door Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P04DC.description: Plug-in and some full hybrids keep the fuel tank sealed while driving, separated from the charcoal canister by a valve. When the driver presses the fuel button, the system opens the valve, lets the pressure escape into the canister and only then unlocks the filler door. A switch reports whether the door is open or closed, so that the tank can be sealed again afterwards. P04DC means the door switch signal is electrically valid but implausible. A GM patent detects refuelling from a rising fuel level at standstill with low tank pressure; if the switch reported open for less than about 20 s, or closed for too long, it is faulty. A Ford patent sets a fault if the fuel level rose and the car drove off without the switch ever reporting open – the valve then stays open and the driver is warned. If the door state is unknown, the system leaves the tank open to the canister as a precaution and suspends the leak tests. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules and patents for the door switch.

causes.label: Switch mechanically jammed or misadjusted (reports one state permanently)
Door or actuator damaged or missing
Signal or connector fault with a valid but wrong level
Fuel level sensor faulty (refuelling misdetected)

symptoms: Fuel door open message although the door is closed, or missing when it is open
Door may not open or only after a delay

P04DD.title: Cold Start EGR A Flow Insufficient Detected
P04DD.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P04DD monitors EGR A while a cold-start emission reduction strategy is active and commands EGR: if the flow does not react as intended, too little exhaust is recirculated in the warm-up phase. CARB requires separate codes for such cold-start faults, which is why P04DD exists alongside P0401. The only manufacturer reference is a FCA bulletin for a six-cylinder diesel with high- and low-pressure EGR, naming it as a consequence of a failed position sensor (P0407/P0408) – repair that first.

causes.label: EGR valve position sensor faulty (follow-on code)
EGR valve sticking or not opening when cold (soot, icing, condensate)
EGR path or cooler narrowed
Pressure, temperature or air mass sensor misreading

symptoms: Higher NOx after a cold start

P04DE.title: Cold Start EGR A Flow Excessive Detected
P04DE.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P04DE is the counterpart of P04DD: during an active cold-start strategy the flow of EGR A is too high – the strategy calls for little or limited EGR, but the valve lets more through. CARB requires separate codes for cold-start faults. No manufacturer document available to us uses P04DE; FCA uses the neighbouring code P04DD, so its use there is plausible but not documented. Too much exhaust in a cold engine causes rough running, smoke and in extreme cases stalling.

causes.label: EGR valve not closing fully (soot, condensate, stuck open)
Position sensor reports a wrong position
Air mass or pressure difference misreading

symptoms: Rough idle after a cold start
Smoke or soot after a cold start (diesel), stalling possible

P04DF.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Performance/Stuck Open
P04DF.description: Purge valve A is the main EVAP purge valve between charcoal canister and intake manifold (on turbo engines the low-load path); its electrical circuit faults are P0443, P0458 and P0459. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows GM's comparable check P0496, Subaru's valve B counterpart P04AE and CARB's purge flow requirement. P04DF means valve A does not react as commanded or lets vapour through when closed: with the system sealed and the valve not driven, vacuum must not reach the tank. Intake vacuum then draws vapour all the time – rich mixture and hard starting after refuelling are typical.

causes.label: Purge valve A leaking or stuck open (charcoal dust or dirt on the seat)
Canister broken down, charcoal dust in the valve
Tank pressure sensor giving a wrong signal
Hoses swapped or wrongly routed

symptoms: Hard starting or stumbling idle right after refuelling

P04E0.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Stuck Closed
P04E0.description: Purge valve A is the main EVAP purge valve between charcoal canister and intake manifold (on turbo engines the low-load path); its electrical circuit faults are P0443, P0458 and P0459. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows GM's comparable check P0496, Subaru's valve B counterpart P04AE and CARB's purge flow requirement. P04E0 means valve A does not open although it is driven: no vacuum builds up in the tank and the mixture does not react while purging – CARB requires missing purge flow to be detected. The canister is then not purged and saturates, causing fuel smell and early nozzle shut-off.

causes.label: Purge valve A stuck closed (gummed, charcoal dust, spring or armature)
Purge line kinked or blocked
Canister or vent blocked
Tank pressure sensor faulty

symptoms: Nozzle clicks off early when refuelling

P04E1.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit
P04E1.description: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) system routes blow-by gas from the crankcase into the intake; CARB requires a disconnection between crankcase and intake to be detected. GM's 2.0-litre LSY has a pressure sensor in the PCV hose: with the hose connected it must see a pressure drop that grows with air flow, plus pressure pulses from the pistons. Ford reports the same sensor type as crankcase pressure sensor A (P051A ff). P04E1 is the sensor's general circuit fault, typical of digital sensors with invalid signal patterns or where low and high are not separated. Its circuit diagnosis is a precondition for the disconnection check P04DB. No manufacturer document available to us uses P04E1 itself; GM uses P04E2/P04E3, Ford P051A ff.

causes.label: Sensor connector not latched or corroded
Signal, 5 V reference or ground wire open
Sensor faulty
Engine module

symptoms: Disconnection check P04DB does not run

P04E2.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit Low
P04E2.description: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) system routes blow-by gas from the crankcase into the intake; CARB requires a disconnection between crankcase and intake to be detected. GM's 2.0-litre LSY has a pressure sensor in the PCV hose: with the hose connected it must see a pressure drop that grows with air flow, plus pressure pulses from the pistons. Ford reports the same sensor type as crankcase pressure sensor A (P051A ff). P04E2 means the sensor signal is too low: GM's LSY sets it at 4.3 % of 5 V or less (about 0.22 V) in 1280 of 1600 samples, MIL after two trips. With this ratiometric sensor an open signal line also reads low, as does a missing 5 V reference. The disconnection check P04DB is then suspended.

causes.label: Signal line open or shorted to ground
5 V reference open or shorted (often shared with other sensors)
Connector not latched or corroded
Sensor faulty

symptoms: Disconnection check P04DB does not run

P04E3.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit High
P04E3.description: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) system routes blow-by gas from the crankcase into the intake; CARB requires a disconnection between crankcase and intake to be detected. GM's 2.0-litre LSY has a pressure sensor in the PCV hose: with the hose connected it must see a pressure drop that grows with air flow, plus pressure pulses from the pistons. Ford reports the same sensor type as crankcase pressure sensor A (P051A ff). P04E3 means the sensor signal is too high: GM's LSY sets it at 95.5 % of 5 V or more (about 4.78 V) in 1280 of 1600 samples, MIL after two trips. Typical is a signal line shorted to 5 V or battery voltage; an open sensor ground can also pull the signal up. The disconnection check P04DB is then suspended.

causes.label: Signal line shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Sensor ground open
Sensor faulty
Corroded or wet connector

symptoms: Disconnection check P04DB does not run

P04E4.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P04E4.description: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) system routes blow-by gas from the crankcase into the intake; CARB requires a disconnection between crankcase and intake to be detected. GM's 2.0-litre LSY has a pressure sensor in the PCV hose: with the hose connected it must see a pressure drop that grows with air flow, plus pressure pulses from the pistons. Ford reports the same sensor type as crankcase pressure sensor A (P051A ff). P04E4 means the sensor signal jumps or drops out briefly – usually a loose contact, a chafed wire or a measuring port blocked by oil sludge or ice. The disconnection check P04DB is then suspended or may report falsely. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows the GM sibling codes P04E2/P04E3 and CARB.

causes.label: Loose contact at the sensor connector
Chafed wire with intermittent short
Sensor faulty or measuring port blocked (oil sludge, ice)
Engine module

symptoms: Disconnection check P04DB does not run

P04E5.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit
P04E5.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. The code standard allows up to four EGR temperature sensors, A to D – for example before and after the cooler, or in the high- and low-pressure circuits; which is which depends on the maker. Sensor D is the fourth of them, usually an NTC whose low voltage means hot. P04E5 is its general circuit fault, conceivable on systems with high- and low-pressure EGR and two sensors per circuit. No manufacturer document available to us uses sensor D – GM, Ford and FCA use at most A to C – so the description follows CARB's requirement to check input circuits for continuity and range. EGR then uses a substitute value or is switched off.

causes.label: Wire or connector fault
Sensor faulty
Engine module

symptoms: Usually no change in driving (EGR on a substitute value or off)
Possibly EGR flow or cooler codes (P0401, P2457)

P04E6.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Range/Performance
P04E6.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Sensor D is the fourth of up to four EGR temperature sensors, conceivable on engines with high- and low-pressure EGR and a sensor before and after each cooler; it is usually an NTC whose low voltage means hot. No manufacturer document available to us uses sensor D; the description follows CARB and Ford's checks on sensor B as a comparison. P04E6 means the signal is electrically valid but implausible – for example it differs from other temperatures after a long stop, does not react when EGR opens, or freezes. Ford compares sensor B with intake and charge air after at least 6 hours off and flags more than 25 °C.

causes.label: Sensor drifting (soot or oil crust, ageing)
Contact resistance in connector or harness (heat, corrosion)
Real temperature deviation: EGR cooler or bypass faulty, valve sticking
Comparison sensor faulty

P04E7.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Low
P04E7.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Sensor D is the fourth of up to four EGR temperature sensors, conceivable on engines with high- and low-pressure EGR and a sensor before and after each cooler; it is usually an NTC whose low voltage means hot. No manufacturer document available to us uses sensor D; the description follows CARB and Ford's checks on sensor B as a comparison. P04E7 means the signal is below its lower limit – a signal line shorted to ground or, theoretically, an extremely high temperature. For sensor B Ford uses below 0.19 V. A substitute value is used and EGR may be reduced.

causes.label: Signal line chafed against ground or the engine
Sensor shorted internally
Water or corrosion in the connector
Module input faulty

P04E8.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit High
P04E8.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Sensor D is the fourth of up to four EGR temperature sensors, conceivable on engines with high- and low-pressure EGR and a sensor before and after each cooler; it is usually an NTC whose low voltage means hot. No manufacturer document available to us uses sensor D; the description follows CARB and Ford's checks on sensor B as a comparison. P04E8 means the signal is above its upper limit – an open circuit in sensor, connector, line or ground, or a short to positive; the reading looks very cold. For sensor B Ford uses above 4.95 V. A substitute value is used.

causes.label: Connector off or loose, or pin corroded
Sensor open internally (heat damage)
Sensor ground line open
Signal line shorted to positive

P04E9.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P04E9.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Sensor D is the fourth of up to four EGR temperature sensors, conceivable on engines with high- and low-pressure EGR and a sensor before and after each cooler; it is usually an NTC whose low voltage means hot. No manufacturer document available to us uses sensor D; the description follows CARB and Ford's checks on sensor B as a comparison. P04E9 means the signal briefly leaves its valid range or changes impossibly fast – typically a loose contact. Ford detects such sporadic faults on other sensors with short limit violations of about 0.4 s.

causes.label: Loose contact in connector or harness (vibration, heat)
Sensor with an internal hairline crack
Chafed harness
Module or ground connection

symptoms: Check engine light on, may come and go

P04EA.title: EVAP System Small Leak Detected - Fuel Tank Side
P04EA.description: Hybrids with a sealed fuel tank have a valve separating the tank from the charcoal canister and its vent side. CARB allows such sections to be leak-checked separately with their own codes; a Ford patent checks the tank side via tank pressure with the valve closed and the canister side with a leak check module. Conventional systems report the same leak as P0442, P0455 or P0456. P04EA reports a small leak (0.040 in) in the tank section – tank, filler neck, cap and lines up to the tank valve. No manufacturer document available to us names this code; the description follows CARB and the Ford patent.

causes.label: Fuel cap or seal leaking or not closed properly (tether trapped)
Filler neck or tank vent line leaking
Sender or pump flange seal leaking
Tank valve or tank pressure sensor faulty

symptoms: Possibly check fuel cap message or slight fuel smell

P04EB.title: EVAP System Small Leak Detected - Fresh Air Side
P04EB.description: Hybrids with a sealed fuel tank have a valve separating the tank from the charcoal canister and its vent side. CARB allows such sections to be leak-checked separately with their own codes; a Ford patent checks the tank side via tank pressure with the valve closed and the canister side with a leak check module. Conventional systems report the same leak as P0442, P0455 or P0456. P04EB reports a small leak (0.040 in) in the canister and vent section – canister, vent valve or leak check module, dust filter and lines up to the purge valve – typically checked with the leak check pump with the engine off. No manufacturer document available to us names this code; the description follows CARB and the Ford patent.

causes.label: Crack or leaking connection at the canister or vent lines
Vent valve or leak check module not sealing
Purge valve leaking
Rodent bite or chafing on lines under the car

symptoms: Possibly check fuel cap message or slight fuel smell

P04EC.title: EVAP System Large Leak Detected - Fuel Tank Side
P04EC.description: Hybrids with a sealed fuel tank have a valve separating the tank from the charcoal canister and its vent side. CARB allows such sections to be leak-checked separately with their own codes; a Ford patent checks the tank side via tank pressure with the valve closed and the canister side with a leak check module. Conventional systems report the same leak as P0442, P0455 or P0456. P04EC reports a large leak in the tank section: it cannot be brought to test pressure or loses it at once – cap missing or open, line off. Stellantis documents it on the Jeep Wrangler 4xe plug-in hybrid only, whose conventional models report P0455; several bulletins name a cap not closed properly or a trapped tether, with a forced leak test via the scan tool.

causes.label: Fuel cap not closed properly or tether trapped
Cap or filler neck sealing surface poor
Recirculation or vent line loose at the quick connector
Tank pressure sensor or valve faulty

symptoms: Check fuel cap message, often right after refuelling

P04ED.title: EVAP System Large Leak Detected - Fresh Air Side
P04ED.description: Hybrids with a sealed fuel tank have a valve separating the tank from the charcoal canister and its vent side. CARB allows such sections to be leak-checked separately with their own codes; a Ford patent checks the tank side via tank pressure with the valve closed and the canister side with a leak check module. Conventional systems report the same leak as P0442, P0455 or P0456. P04ED reports a large leak in the canister and vent section: the leak check module builds up no meaningful vacuum – line off, canister broken, vent valve open. Purging may be suspended. No manufacturer document available to us names this code; the description follows CARB and the Ford patent.

causes.label: Line at the canister or leak check module off or broken
Vent valve or leak check module not closing
Canister housing cracked
Purge valve stuck open

symptoms: Possibly check fuel cap message or slight fuel smell

P04EE.title: EVAP System Very Small Leak Detected - Fuel Tank Side
P04EE.description: Hybrids with a sealed fuel tank have a valve separating the tank from the charcoal canister and its vent side. CARB allows such sections to be leak-checked separately with their own codes; a Ford patent checks the tank side via tank pressure with the valve closed and the canister side with a leak check module. Conventional systems report the same leak as P0442, P0455 or P0456. P04EE reports a very small leak (0.020 in) in the tank section, usually checked with the engine off. Stellantis documents it on the Jeep Wrangler 4xe – cap, tether or filler tube, with a scan-tool leak test before replacing parts – and Ford on the C-Max, Fusion and MKZ hybrids and Energi of 2013–17, together with P0456 and P0457, fixed by a tighter purge valve and software.

causes.label: Fuel cap seal deformed or dirty, tether trapped
Purge valve not sealing (Ford hybrids) – plus software
Leaking quick connector or vent line at the tank
Hairline crack in tank lines or flange seal

P04EF.title: EVAP System Very Small Leak Detected - Fresh Air Side
P04EF.description: Hybrids with a sealed fuel tank have a valve separating the tank from the charcoal canister and its vent side. CARB allows such sections to be leak-checked separately with their own codes; a Ford patent checks the tank side via tank pressure with the valve closed and the canister side with a leak check module. Conventional systems report the same leak as P0442, P0455 or P0456. P04EF reports a very small leak (0.020 in) in the canister and vent section; the leak check module compares the vacuum against a 0.020 in reference and the section does not reach it. On Ford's C-Max, Fusion and MKZ hybrids and Energi a leaking purge valve is the typical trigger, fixed per bulletin with the valve and software.

causes.label: Purge valve not sealing
Vent valve or leak check module leaking
Hairline crack or leaking connections at the canister
Module software (misjudgement)

P04F0.title: EVAP System High Load Purge Line A Performance
P04F0.description: Turbocharged engines also purge the charcoal canister under boost, through a high-load line to the compressor inlet via a venturi; check valves keep boost out of the EVAP system, and CARB requires this path to be monitored. P04F0 checks it: Ford (2020–23, replacing P144C) runs the test once per trip under boost with the vent closed and purge open, and sets the code if tank pressure rises faster than 0.5 or 1 inH2O/s or the vacuum rate is out of range, within 5–10 s. VW, Audi and Bentley monitor the line with their own pressure sensor.

causes.label: Check valve in the purge line leaking, stuck open, fitted wrongly or missing
High-load purge line to the turbo or venturi off, cracked or blocked
Purge line pressure sensor wrongly connected or faulty (VW group)
Purge valve or venturi faulty

symptoms: Possibly fuel smell, EVAP readiness not set

P04F1.title: EVAP System Purge Line Performance
P04F1.description: P04F1 is the function check of a purge line that is not the high-load path A – by the wording of another code list the low-pressure path to the intake manifold, counterpart of P04F0. The purge valve opens and the tank pressure or mixture reaction is missing or wrong: the line is blocked or off, or a check valve sticks. CARB requires every purge path to be checked; a FCA patent describes such a stepwise test. No manufacturer document available to us names this code.

causes.label: Purge line to the intake manifold off, kinked or blocked
Check valve in the low-load path sticking
Purge valve not opening fully
Tank pressure sensor misreading

P04F2.title: Catalyst Heater Supply Voltage Bank 1
P04F2.description: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of the catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start; Emitec's EMICAT runs on 12, 24 or 48 V and draws up to about 300 A. It is in series production on 48-volt mild-hybrid diesel vans since 2022. P04F2 concerns the heated catalyst of bank 1. The code monitors the supply voltage of the heater: if it lies outside its window when heating is requested, the heater cannot deliver its power and is limited or switched off, so the catalyst lights off later. A Subaru patent detects faults in the supply path when the heater is commanded. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – Ford, for example, states that heated catalyst monitoring is not supported – so thresholds and warning-lamp logic are not documented; the description follows CARB and patents for the same part.

causes.label: 48 V or high-voltage supply weak (battery, charge, cold, DC-DC converter)
Fuse, relay or power switch faulty
Contact resistance or corrosion at high-current connector or ground
Module or voltage measurement faulty

symptoms: Check engine light on (depending on the maker)
Higher emissions after a cold start

P04F4.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Low Bank 1

P04F6.description: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of the catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start; Emitec's EMICAT runs on 12, 24 or 48 V and draws up to about 300 A. The code means the measured voltage in the heater circuit is too high for the commanded state – a short to the supply, a sticking switch or, if measured on the low side, an open heating element. The heater is switched off or runs uncontrolled. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – Ford, for example, states that heated catalyst monitoring is not supported – so thresholds and warning-lamp logic are not documented; the description follows CARB and patents for the same part.

Heating element or feed open (crack, electrode damage)
Relay or power switch sticking
Corroded connector

symptoms: Check engine light on (depending on the maker)
Higher emissions after a cold start

P04FA.title: EGR A Control Temperature Too High
P04FA.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P04FA is a protective check of the electrically driven EGR valve A (DC motor on an H-bridge with position sensor): the module detects overtemperature or thermal overload of the actuator, modelled from current, actuating work and position behaviour, and limits or switches off EGR. Ford petrol engines from 2020 run it continuously with 4 s to fault above 8.25 V and 400 rpm. Pierburg documents heat damage to VW's 12 V electric EGR valves. EGR then closes, NOx rises.

causes.label: EGR valve stiff from coking (motor working against resistance)
High thermal load (full load, poor valve cooling, low coolant)
Valve motor or H-bridge driver faulty (overcurrent)
Module software

symptoms: Rough idle or jerking if the valve hangs
Loss of power, possibly limp mode

P04FB.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Range/Performance
P04FB.description: The crankcase ventilation hose connection sensor is a pressure sensor in the PCV line that measures pressure relative to atmosphere; it is the basis for detecting a disconnected hose (P04DB). P04FB is its plausibility check: GM's 2.0-litre LSY checks the zero point with the engine stopped (at least 10 s, coolant 70 °C or more) – a reading outside ±0.63 kPa or a frozen value sets the code in 128 of 160 samples, MIL after two trips. The disconnection check P04DB is then not possible.

causes.label: Pressure sensor drifting (zero point error)
Sensor port or line blocked by oil or ice (value frozen)
Contact resistance in supply, ground or signal
Residual crankcase pressure after switch-off (blocked ventilation)

P04FC.title: Crankcase Ventilation System Performance
P04FC.description: The crankcase ventilation routes blow-by gas into the intake, and CARB requires it to be monitored. P04FC is a general function check: pressure or flow in the system deviates from the model. FCA uses it on the 2.0-litre turbo in the Wrangler and Cherokee (2018–19) and the 3.6 Pentastar in the Challenger (2020), with known false triggers fixed by engine module software; the strategy is not published, a FCA patent evaluates a pressure sensor in the fresh-air line.

causes.label: Module software (FCA false trigger)
PCV valve or oil separator blocked or sticking
Ventilation or fresh-air hose leaking or loose, oil filler cap leaking
Increased blow-by (piston rings)

symptoms: Possibly oil consumption or oil in the intake

P04FD.title: EGR Actuator A Control Processor Performance
P04FD.description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Some EGR actuators have their own electronics (smart actuators), with position control inside the actuator and communication with the engine module by bus or PWM. P04FD means the actuator reports an internal processor or electronics fault, or its self-test failed. CARB does not require such internal faults to be reported, so the code is a voluntary detail. Volvo and Mack trucks with turbocompound document it with false triggers fixed by engine software. The actuator then goes to its default position and EGR is off.

causes.label: Engine or actuator software (false trigger)
Electronics in the EGR actuator faulty (heat, moisture)
Actuator supply or ground unstable
Valve stiff, causing a control fault in the actuator

P04FE.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Performance Bank 1
P04FE.description: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of the catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start; Emitec's EMICAT runs on 12, 24 or 48 V and draws up to about 300 A. It is in series production on 48-volt mild-hybrid diesel vans since 2022. P04FE concerns the heated catalyst of bank 1. The code is the function check: the circuit is electrically sound but the effect does not fit – for example the energy delivered in a time window after switch-on stays below target, which a Toyota patent evaluates as a ratio, or the catalyst temperature does not rise as modelled. Ageing of the disc raises its resistance. The pure temperature result code is P0424/P0434. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – Ford, for example, states that heated catalyst monitoring is not supported – so thresholds and warning-lamp logic are not documented; the description follows CARB and patents for the same part.

causes.label: Heating disc aged (resistance increased, cracks, electrode damage)
Supply drops under load (cold or weak 48 V battery, contact resistance)
Catalyst or exhaust temperature sensor implausible
Software or calibration

symptoms: Check engine light on (depending on the maker)
Higher emissions after a cold start
